identification.summary: Grayling is the name Symantec's Threat Hunter Team (Broadcom) gave to a previously unseen threat actor, reported in October 2023, that targeted organizations mainly in Taiwan [S1][S2]. Its distinctive trait is DLL side-loading through the exported function SbieDll_Hook to load payloads such as Cobalt Strike, NetSpy and the Havoc framework [S2][S4].
identification.notes: Symantec reported the activity running from February 2023 to at least May 2023 [S2][S3]. Symantec reported no overlap with Naikon, which had used similar SbieDll_Hook/SandboxieBITS.exe side-loading [S2]. No Microsoft name or MITRE ATT&CK group ID was found in the sources reviewed.

attribution.confidence: Symantec did not tie Grayling to a specific country; it said the Taiwan focus suggests a region with strategic interest in Taiwan [S2][S4]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Symantec's reasoning rests on the heavy Taiwan targeting, with DLL side-loading noted as common among China-linked actors, while it found no overlap with Naikon [S2][S4]. The China-linked label is a press inference, not a vendor or government attribution [S4].

objectives: Symantec assessed the targets and post-exploitation behaviors as consistent with intelligence gathering rather than financial motivation; no data exfiltration was observed [S3][S4].

targeting.notes: Primary focus was Taiwanese manufacturing, IT and biomedical organizations; a Pacific Islands government agency and organizations in Vietnam and the US were also reportedly targeted [S2][S3]. SC Media's summary describes the island target as unspecified [S6].

capabilities.summary: Initial access was likely via exploitation of public-facing web servers, sometimes with web shells deployed, rather than spear phishing [S4]. Payloads were loaded by DLL side-loading via SbieDll_Hook, delivering Cobalt Strike, NetSpy and the open-source Havoc C2 framework [S2][S3]. Reported additional activity includes Mimikatz credential dumping, Active Directory discovery, exploitation of CVE-2019-0803 for privilege escalation, and terminating processes listed in a file named processlist.txt [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Taiwan-focused intrusion set
campaigns.summary: Symantec observed Grayling intrusions from February 2023 through at least May 2023 against manufacturing, IT and biomedical organizations in Taiwan, with a Pacific Islands government agency and entities in Vietnam and the US also reportedly targeted [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Public disclosure by Symantec
campaigns.summary: Symantec publicly reported Grayling as a previously unseen actor, citing the SbieDll_Hook side-loading technique and no observed exfiltration [S1][S2][S4].

diamond.adversary: Unattributed actor named Grayling by Symantec; Symantec did not name a country [S2][S4].
diamond.capability: Web shells, DLL side-loading via SbieDll_Hook, Cobalt Strike, Havoc, NetSpy, Mimikatz, CVE-2019-0803 exploit [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Taiwanese manufacturing, IT and biomedical organizations; a Pacific Islands government agency; entities in Vietnam and the US [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Symantec said the Taiwan focus suggests a region with strategic interest in Taiwan; intelligence gathering was the assessed motive [S3][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing web servers (likely initial access vector) and Windows hosts/Active Directory environments [S2][S3][S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the reported target set (Taiwanese manufacturing, IT, biomedical; Pacific Islands government) places internet-facing web servers and AD-joined Windows hosts as relevant terrain [S2][S3][S4]. Step 3: the actor is credible at web-server exploitation, side-loaded Cobalt Strike/Havoc/NetSpy, and credential theft, with no exfiltration observed [S2][S3]. MLCOA: continued espionage-style access against Taiwan-linked organizations via public-facing servers. MDCOA: exploitation of regional partner or supplier networks (Pacific, Vietnam, US) as stepping stones; this is inference not stated in sources. Candidate indicators: new web shells on external servers, legitimate-looking binaries loading DLLs exporting SbieDll_Hook, Havoc/Cobalt Strike beacons, processes terminated per processlist.txt [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: share SbieDll_Hook side-loading and web-shell detection content with defenders of regional partner and supplier networks. Authorities: confirm which entities fall under DODIN-A versus partner or commercial ownership before any response action. Mission assurance: prioritize patching and monitoring of internet-facing servers and AD credential hygiene on mission-relevant systems. Coordination: route vendor reporting (Symantec) through intelligence and cyber protection teams and coordinate with partners in the Indo-Pacific region.

provenance.importedSummary: Grayling activity was first observed in early 2023, when a number of victims were identified with distinctive malicious DLL side-loading activity. Grayling appears to target organisations in Asia, however one unknown organisation in the United States was also targeted. Industries targeted include Biomedical, Government and Information Technology. Grayling use a variety of tools during their attacks, including well known tools such as Cobalt Strike and Havoc and also some others.
